record.original_question: Quantify the aging phenomenon of ideal fluids, preferably by constructing a Lyapunov function on fluid velocities that is nondecreasing along Euler evolution except on a slim exceptional set.

evidence.quote: Problem 22 (Aging Problem). Is it possible to quantify the “aging” property of the fluid? Perhaps the best way is to find a Lyapunov function L defined and continuous on the space of fluid velocities in Te Dµs such that dt d L(u(t, ·)) ≥ 0 where u is a solution of (1.1) with equality holding on a “slim” subset of Te Dµ (say, of infinite codimension). s The first Lyapunov function in this context was constructed by Yudovich in 1970s for flows with a rectilinear streamline (e.g., flows in domains whose boundary contains a straight line segment), see [147, 149]. The construction was subsequently generalized for arbitrary bounded domains in [110]. It implies “regularity deterioration” at least on the boundary. It is natural to expect that there are also Lyapunov functions which are supported inside the fluid domain. Examples describing evolution of weak singularities in the Lagrangian flow were found in [128]. The fact that these singularities become gradually “sharper” as the fluid evolves suggests the same deterioration phenomenon stressed by Yudovich. Consider an ideal fluid in a periodic channel M = T × (0, a). Assume that its initial velocity u0 is C 1 close to that of a plane-parallel flow whose velocity profile v = v(x2 ) satisfies v 0 > 0 and v 00 > 0 in (0, a). Suppose that the level lines of ω0 = curl u0 satisfy ∇ω0 6= 0 in M and that one of the lines ω0 = const has a “kink”.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary (e.g.\ a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ or the periodic channel $\mathbb{T}\times(0,a)$), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving Sobolev diffeomorphisms of $M$ of class $H^s$ (with $s>n/2+1$). The tangent space at the identity may be identified with the space of divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$,
$$T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)=\{u\in H^s(M;TM):\ \operatorname{div} u=0,\ u\cdot\nu|_{\partial M}=0\},$$
on which the incompressible Euler equations
$$\partial_t u+(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla p,\qquad \operatorname{div} u=0,\qquad u\cdot\nu|_{\partial M}=0 \tag{$\ast$}$$
define a (local) flow $u(t,\cdot)$.

Construct a continuous functional ("Lyapunov function") 
$$L:T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}$$
with the following two properties:

(i) For every solution $u(t,\cdot)$ of $(\ast)$, the map $t\mapsto L(u(t,\cdot))$ is monotone nondecreasing, i.e.\ $\frac{d}{dt}L(u(t,\cdot))\ge 0$ for all $t$ for which the solution is defined.

(ii) The set of velocity fields $u\in T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ at which equality $\frac{d}{dt}L(u(t,\cdot))=0$ may hold is a "slim" subset of $T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ — for instance, of infinite codimension.

Such a functional should quantify the heuristic "aging"/regularity-deterioration phenomenon for ideal incompressible fluids and, in particular, should not be supported only near $\partial M$ (i.e.\ examples with support in the interior of the fluid domain are sought). Does such a Lyapunov function exist?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of constructing a global Lyapunov function on divergence-free velocity fields that is monotone along Euler evolution outside a slim set is listed as an open problem in the geometric-hydrodynamics open-problems survey (Khesin et al., 2022). Partial results exist: Yudovich (1970s) constructed local Lyapunov functions for flows with a rectilinear streamline, and Shnirelman extended this to arbitrary bounded domains, both implying regularity deterioration near the boundary. No interior-supported global Lyapunov function quantifying aging is known.
